count_note: 41 items. Section B: 18 questions (Q1-Q18; the table has 18 rows). B2 has 17 rows because Q15 and Q18 share one; each decision is settled under its question, and for each I say whether today's code follows it. 'Wyjaśnione' explains Q1, Q12 and Q13 and adds no item. Q3, Q4, Q10, Q11, Q13, Q15, Q16 and Q17 overlap A14, A26, A13, A13, A8, A20, A5/LIVE-001 and A15 of the first-session file: I settle them from section B's side with a re-check, not a redo. LIVE-findings.md: 9 items besides LIVE-001, LIVE-002 and LIVE-003 (which are settled in the first-session file): the suite claim of its first section (LF-SUITE), the R9 gap inside LIVE-001 (LF-R9, its own claim with its own recommendation), the six bullets of 'Co WERYFIKALNIE działa dobrze' (LF-DEATH, LF-REMNANT, LF-PERMS, LF-VOTE, LF-CLEANUP, LF-NOTHROW) and the LIVEKIT note under LIVE-002 (LF-LIVEKIT). The parts of LIVE-003 (the invariant that read only the constant; the reroll road) are LIVE-003's and stay in the first-session file. AUDIT-1.1.88.md: 14 items besides its four findings: the 3 bullets of 'Obszary wymagające żywego oka' (OA-1..OA-3); 8 of the 9 bullets of 'Co zweryfikowanie działa dobrze' (WD-WRITE, WD-HTML, WD-ROLLS, WD-CRIME, WD-GEAR, WD-ROOMS, WD-DEGRADE, WD-SUITE; the ninth, Remnant redaction, is the same claim as LF-REMNANT and is settled there; WD-CRIME and WD-SUITE overlap LIVE-findings.md and are kept as rows because 1.1.88 words and counts them differently); and checklist items 5 (two suggestions: CL-CHANGELOG, CL-POLISH) and 6 (CL-LIVE, a dedup of OA-1..3). Checklist items 1-4 are the four findings. The verdict's grades and its '147 scenariuszy' are no items; the latter is noted under LF-SUITE. Checklist item 6 says 'cztery obszary' while the section has three bullets. Total 18 + 9 + 14 = 41. For a claim of what worked (a strength, a note), status reads: fixed = the claim still holds on today's code, nothing to put right; partly = part holds, part no longer does or was replaced by a decision; open = not re-established (LF-NOTHROW) - never a defect found by me; obsolete = its subject was replaced. For a live area, partly = some readings exist on a real Foundry, open = none.

l1.what: Whether another player's screen draws the dragged token's ruler (path and distance) during an Eclipse on Foundry 14.370
recipe: Start an Eclipse with the GM and two players connected, room visibility on.
Player A drags their student's token across two rooms, holding the drag for a few seconds.
Player B, watching the same scene, records whether any line, waypoint or distance label is drawn for A's token, and whether A's token itself is drawn.
On A's console: `canvas.tokens.controlled[0].ruler?.visible` during the drag; on B's console the same for A's token object.
l1.settles_if: Settled fixed if B sees no ruler and no token for the whole drag; open (minor) if B sees the path or distance.

new_observations.title: trial-floor.mjs's header says a rebuttal 'returns to open debate by itself'; the code ends the floor
new_observations.what: The header's table of modes: 'rebuttal the objector AND the person they aimed at, for two minutes. Nobody else. Then it returns to open debate by itself.' The machine: `if (floor.mode === MODES.rebuttal) return inRound ? nextTurn(floor, now, cards, ctx) : ended(cards, true);` and `ended` answers `{ floor: null, cards, again: true }` - the floor closes and the console's next step is 'Open the debate again' (floor-machine.mjs:402-406). The same file says so further down: trial-floor.mjs:1652 'A REBUTTAL ENDS THE FLOOR (Dawid, 28.08), rather than dropping back into an open debate.' R1030 pins the code's behaviour.
new_observations.failure_scenario: A developer reading the top of trial-floor.mjs expects a rebuttal to hand the floor back to a running debate and writes a change on that belief, while the GM's console in fact shows 'Open the debate again' after every rebuttal.

new_observations.title: trial-floor.mjs:74 calls FLOOR_MODES 'The three modes' over a table of nine
new_observations.what: `/** The three modes, spelled out once so nothing else has to spell them (floor-machine.mjs `MODES`, since E70 C1). */ export const FLOOR_MODES = MODES;` - MODES holds debate, objection, rebuttal, testimony, panic, closing and the zone modes straw, dive and scrum (lang/en.json DRPG.Floor.mode.* has nine keys). The header's 'So there are three MODES instead' (:18) is the history of Q14's decision and is followed by the newer modes' notes; the JSDoc at :74 is a present-tense count.
new_observations.failure_scenario: A reader of FLOOR_MODES's JSDoc writes a check over 'the three modes' and misses six, the rounds and the zone modes among them.

new_observations.title: config.mjs's TRIAL.speakSeconds is described as 'How long a free discussion runs', the word Q14 reserved for no floor at all
new_observations.what: 'How long a free discussion runs before the bar turns red ... the trial now opens as a free discussion that anyone may speak in, and this is the GM's default budget for it' over `speakSeconds: 180`. After Q14 (B2, 02.09.2026) and trial-floor.mjs:1655-1659, a timed floor anyone may speak in is a debate, and 'discussion' is the trial with no floor open, which has no clock.
new_observations.failure_scenario: A developer looking for the debate's default budget searches config.mjs for 'debate', finds only debateMinSeconds, and takes speakSeconds, described as the discussion's, for something else.
